observation_summary: The compiler fails to report a type-checking error for an invalid property access when it occurs inside a for-loop within a prototype function, whereas it correctly identifies the error in other contexts.
reasoning_summary: The issue is a failure in the type-checking algorithm to correctly propagate or validate property existence within specific control flow structures (loops) inside prototype methods. This is a procedural logic error in the type-checking engine's traversal or validation strategy, rather than a missing guard (Checking) or a simple value assignment error. It is not a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object) because the type-checking capability exists and works in other contexts.
evidence_used: bug_report_description: invalid property not erroring in for loop in prototype function
evidence_gaps: The specific internal logic of the type-checking traversal is not provided in the snippets, only the test cases and the assertion failures.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the compiler is 'missing' a check, the root cause is the algorithmic failure to correctly identify the property context within the loop, not just a missing conditional guard.
The type-checking capability is present and functional in the system; it is failing only in specific, complex code structures.
